finding_key: .github/workflows/agent-iterate-ci.yml::allowed_bots re-enables the autonomous fixer agents, whose prompts/instructions pull in world-writable pr-thread text while a contents:write app token sits in .git/config
evidence: Verified each mechanical premise: agent-iterate-ci.yml ~line 160 adds `allowed_bots`, which by the PR's own comment is what un-blocks the previously-refused bot-initiated fixer run; the prompt just below directs the agent to "reply in the PR's verification thread" and `claude_args` grants unrestricted `Bash`; and the preceding `actions/checkout@v4` (ref head_branch, token = App token) omits `persist-credentials: false`, so the installation token is written into .git/config in the same workspace where branch `postinstall` and the agent run. The same shape holds for the review-panel `fix` job, while the sibling review job explicitly sets `persist-credentials: false` citing this exact exfiltration path, and the issue-spec ingestion applies an `agent:candidate`+non-Bot provenance filter that no PR-thread text passes through. Confidence is medium, not high, because the prompts interpolate only trusted data (harness diagnosis / panel check summaries) — untrusted comment text reaches the agent only if it fetches the thread or if claude-code-action pulls PR context for workflow_run, and `action.yml` was not supplied; the design doc also already accepts secret exposure in these code-executing jobs, making this a hardening gap on a documented risk surface.
